# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 22

**1** Jesus saw some infants [коуі] who were being suckled [соує].

**2** He said to his disciples: "These infants being suckled are like those who enter the kingdom."

**3** They said to him: "So shall we enter the kingdom as little children?"

**4** Jesus said to them: "When you make the two one [оуа], and when you make the inside [нноун] like the outside [нвол] and the outside like the inside [нноун], and the above like the below [псос],

**5** and when you make the male [хоут] and the female one [оуа] and the same [оуоот], so that the male will not be male nor the female female;

**6** and when you fashion eyes [вал] in place of an eye [вал], and a hand [чіж] in place of a hand, and a foot [оуерите] in place of a foot, and an image [хіконе] in place of an image [хіконе] —

**7** then you will enter [вок нноун] the kingdom."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *соує*: to nurse, suckle; the image of complete dependence and nourishment
- *нноун / нвол*: inside / outside — both must become the same (cf. Saying 3)
- *псос*: below, beneath — the above/below pair
- *хоут*: male; *сhіме*: female — the binary to be transcended
- *хіконе*: image, icon; Greek loan-word εἰκών — to fashion a new image is to achieve the divine image
- The transformations: binary → unity (inside/outside, above/below, male/female, part/whole)
- "When you make the two one" — echoes Saying 11 (you were one, became two) in reverse; here the two are made one again
- This is the most complete statement of the Thomas unification ideal

---
